# Storyboard — Rafael Costa, "The Pipeline"

Concept: `concepts.md`, Concept A. Decisions behind this script: `decided-for-you.md`.

## Waiting on Rafael

1. Helix reporting-time reduction: 40% or 60%, and what it actually measures.
2. Lisbon Rent Map traffic: 5,000 or 3,000 visitors/month, and the source of that number.
3. MSc end date: 2021 or 2022.
4. "200+ staff" at Meridian — counted how, by whom.
5. "35% efficiency" at Meridian — efficiency in what, his result or his team's.
6. His part in the Journal of Genomic Methods paper, and whether to name/link it.
7. FraudShield — ever run for real, solo or with others, anything to show.
8. AutoPilot — tied to Meridian or independent, still running, anything to show.
9. Lisbon Rent Map — solo, and the real URL (not the placeholder).
10. What DataTugas actually was.
11. What he built at the Health Data Hackathon, solo or team.
12. A yes (or no) on publishing Beatriz Lima's quote under her name.
13. Whether any employer dashboard may be shown — currently moot, since none depicts one.
14. A real contact email, and any real links (GitHub, the actual rent-map URL).

None of these block reading this plan. They block two things once building starts: the headline stat (point 1–5, 7–9), and one chapter (12).

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sources | Opening + Who | "Rafael Costa — Founder & Product Analyst. I make dashboards people actually use." | Scattered points of raw data drift together into the first row of clean source blocks | Scroll to begin; a nav rail with jumps to every chapter and a skip-to-contact link |
| 2 | Staging | Where from | Employers and schools, each with its years | The nine blocks line up left to right as a timeline, one per entry, ordered by date | Hover a block for its full dates; tap on phone |
| 3 | Intermediate | How | His tools: SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, dbt, Statistics | Blocks regroup into a loose cluster, each face carrying one tool's name | Hover/tap a tool, no further detail (none given) |
| 4 | Marts | What | FraudShield, AutoPilot, Lisbon Rent Map — one line each, as given | Blocks merge into three larger shapes, one per project, each with its own motif (shield / flow / map) | Click a mart to open its one-line detail; "to confirm" chip shows where a figure or screenshot is still pending |
| 5 | Tests | What came of it + What others say | "6+ years · 3 employers · 3 projects built outside work." Winner, Health Data Hackathon 2023. Beatriz Lima's line, held pending confirmation. | A row of small checkmarked nodes lights up one at a time; the quote node is present but dimmed/marked until confirmed | Hover the quote node to see its pending state in a build preview; nothing of the sort shows once live and confirmed |
| 6 | Exposures | The close | The answer: "Trusted, because someone checked." Contact. | All nine blocks reassemble into the full lineage, whole again; the final node pulses | Contact link, CV (later), link back to top |

## Someone with thirty seconds

The first screen (Sources) carries his name, his title, and his own line about what he does. The nav rail is visible immediately with a jump to every chapter and one link that skips straight to Exposures/Contact. Proof — "6+ years · 3 employers · 3 projects built outside work" — sits in Tests, one rail-jump away.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The same six chapters, same order, same text. The node graph becomes a simple vertical connected-dot timeline (flat CSS/SVG, not WebGL), single column, larger tap targets, no camera movement — just scroll-triggered fades between settled states. |
| With reduced motion | No camera moves and no parallax. Each chapter appears as a static settled state with a plain crossfade. All text and all blocks' content are still present. |
| With no WebGL | The same flat 2D version used on phones: an SVG/CSS pipeline diagram standing in for the 3D blocks, same labels, same order, same copy. |
| With no JavaScript | A plain HTML document: six headed sections in the chapters' order (Sources, Staging, Intermediate, Marts, Tests, Exposures), all text and project lines present, static illustration in place of the node graph, no animation. |

## The look and the type

**Primary look — "Night pipeline."** Ground: near-black charcoal. Ink: warm off-white. One accent: copper/terracotta, a nod to Lisbon rooftops rather than a default SaaS blue-purple. Node surfaces: dark brushed graphite with thin edge-lit lines.

**Alternate — "Azulejo."** Ground: deep indigo. Ink: chalk white. Accent: gold edge lines. Node surfaces: matte, ceramic-tile-like. Held in reserve; properly chosen by scrolling the built site, not from swatches.

Two typefaces: a humanist grotesk for body text (e.g. Inter or General Sans), and a monospace for anything printed on the pipeline blocks (e.g. IBM Plex Mono) — because the real material of his trade's documents is code and config, which is set in monospace.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — nav rail with chapter jumps + scroll progress | Me (taste) |
| A page for each project | Later — start with the in-page mart tiles; split out only if he wants deeper case studies and more material | Me (taste) |
| Every project listed | Build — a plain flat appendix/CV-style list, for anyone who skips the 3D | Me (taste) |
| How to reach them, and a CV | Build the contact method; CV download later | Contact: waiting on him for a real address. CV: later, me |
| What others say | Build the chapter; Beatriz Lima's quote held pending her/his confirmation | Waiting on him |
| Languages | Later — English first since all material given is in English; Portuguese after | Me (taste) |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build — a generated OG card (name + line) and a simple favicon from the pipeline motif | Me (taste) |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — an on-brand 404 ("no data found for this address") | Me (taste) |
| A blog | Never — nothing in the material suggests he writes | Me (taste), revisit if told otherwise |
| A chat | Never — no stated need | Me (taste) |
| A legal notice | Build, minimal — Portugal/EU; only if any analytics or cookies are used | Me (taste) |

## What I'm asking for

Not a yes to build yet — this plan is the deliverable for now. When you have ten minutes this week or next, the fourteen items under "Waiting on Rafael" are what would sharpen it before anyone builds anything. Anything you don't get to just stays marked "to confirm" and stays off the parts of the page that would stand on it.

Good — going with **The Pipeline**. Here's the full script, still nothing built.

## Fourteen things still unconfirmed
These don't block this plan, but they're why some faces carry a "to confirm" chip instead of a number, and why one chapter is dimmed: the 40%/60% and 5,000/3,000 figures, the 200+ and 35% claims and what they measure, your part in the genomics paper, whether FraudShield/AutoPilot/Rent Map ever ran for real and solo or not, what DataTugas was, what you built at the hackathon, the MSc end year, a yes on publishing Beatriz Lima's quote by name, and a real contact email/links.

## The object
Nine identical blocks, like pipeline nodes, joined by edges. The same nine blocks regroup through every chapter; at rest they sit as a layered lineage, raw at the bottom, exposed at the top.

## The scroll, in full

**1 — Sources** *(opens, and who)*
- *Scatter:* nine points, loose and unconnected, drifting. Nothing on their faces yet — just raw, unformed texture. Caption: "Rafael Costa — Founder & Product Analyst." / "I make dashboards people actually use."
- *Gather:* the points pull into one loose row, block shapes forming, faint edges starting to draw. Caption: the question — "What turns raw numbers into something people actually trust?"

**2 — Staging** *(where from)*
- *Timeline:* the row lines up left to right by date — Atlantico Telecom (summer 2020), DataTugas (Oct 2018–Jun 2020), Universidade do Douro twice (BSc 2017–2020, MSc 2020–), Helix Genomics Institute (Sep 2021–Jan 2024), Meridian Bank (Feb 2024–present). A thin "now" line slides across as you scroll. Caption: "Six years, five stops: telecom, a venture of his own, genomics, banking." *Click:* hover/tap any block for its full dates.

**3 — Intermediate** *(how)*
- *Cluster:* blocks loosen into an orbiting cluster, one tool per face — SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, dbt, Statistics. Faint lines connect down to the timeline below. Caption: "The tools behind it." No further detail — none is in the material.

**4 — Marts** *(what)*
- *Split:* nine blocks separate into three groups of three, merging into three larger shapes — FraudShield (shield motif, "real-time fraud detection system"), AutoPilot (flow motif, "automation platform for analytics teams"), Lisbon Rent Map (map motif, "a map of what a room costs in every parish of Lisbon"). A small "to confirm" chip floats by whichever fact is still unconfirmed. *Click:* a group fans open to show its one-liner expanded — same words, nothing invented.

**5 — Tests** *(what came of it, what others say)*
- *Checks:* a row of small nodes lights up one at a time on scroll — "6+ years · 3 employers · 3 projects built outside work," "Winner, Health Data Hackathon 2023."
- *Quote:* one block tilts forward like a plaque, carrying Beatriz Lima's line — shown dimmed and marked pending until you confirm it can go up under her name. If you never confirm, it becomes an unattributed paraphrase instead of disappearing.

**6 — Exposures** *(the close)*
- *Reassemble:* all nine blocks return to the full lineage, whole again, final node glowing "Exposed." Caption: the answer — "Trusted, because someone checked."
- *Contact:* settled, static — contact method, links, CV once you give me one. *Click:* contact link, back-to-top.

Nav rail (jump to any chapter) and a skip-to-contact link are visible from the very first screen.

## Look and type
**Night pipeline:** near-black charcoal ground, warm off-white text, one copper/terracotta accent — a Lisbon-rooftop nod rather than default SaaS blue-purple. Node surfaces: dark brushed graphite, thin edge-lit lines. Body text in a humanist grotesk (Inter-like); anything printed on the blocks in monospace (your trade's real documents are code and config). An alternate dark-indigo "Azulejo" look stays in reserve, to be picked by scrolling the real thing once it exists, not from swatches now.

## Phone, and without the 3D
Same six chapters, same order, same words, always — the text is ordinary HTML over the scene, never scroll-only.
- **Phone:** the node graph becomes a flat vertical connected-dot timeline, single column, larger tap targets, scroll-triggered fades instead of camera moves.
- **Reduced motion:** no camera movement or parallax — each chapter settles in with a plain crossfade.
- **No WebGL:** the same flat version phones get — an SVG/CSS pipeline diagram standing in for the 3D blocks.
- **No JavaScript:** a plain HTML page, six headed sections in order, static illustration instead of the graph, no animation — everything still readable.

| | Build / later / never |
|---|---|
| Nav rail + scroll progress | Build |
| Per-project subpages | Later — only if you want deeper case studies |
| Flat appendix list of everything (for recruiters skipping the 3D) | Build |
| Contact method | Build, but waiting on a real address from you |
| CV download | Later |
| "What others say" chapter | Build; Beatriz's quote held pending her/your confirmation |
| Portuguese translation | Later |
| Social share preview card + favicon | Build |
| On-brand 404 | Build |
| Blog | Never — nothing in your material points to it |
| Chat widget | Never |
| Minimal Portugal/EU privacy notice | Build, if any analytics/cookies are used |

Full detail is saved in `docs/story/storyboard.md` (now with every beat), `concepts.md`, `decided-for-you.md`, and `facts.md`. Still no building — say yes and tell me when you've had a chance to look at the fourteen open items, and that's the next step.

## Phone, and without the 3D
Same six chapters, same order, same words, always — the text is ordinary HTML over the scene, never scroll-only.
- **Phone:** the node graph becomes a flat vertical connected-dot timeline, single column, larger tap targets, scroll-triggered fades instead of camera moves.
- **Reduced motion:** no camera movement or parallax — each chapter settles in with a plain crossfade.
- **No WebGL:** the same flat version phones get — an SVG/CSS pipeline diagram standing in for the 3D blocks.
- **No JavaScript:** a plain HTML page, six headed sections in order, static illustration instead of the graph, no animation — everything still readable.
